feedback.problem:
If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-2$ and $f(-2)=2,$ then what is the value of

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)}({(f(x))}^{2}+4)\,?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We're told that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-2.$ According to the definition of continuity, this means that ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)$ exists and

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=f(-2)=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2)}({(f(x))}^{2}+4) & =({2}^{2}+4)=8.\end{aligned}
$$
